Concord MCP 

 Let Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, Goose, GitHub Copilot CLI, and OpenCode talk to each other. 

 
 The open-source, local-first communication and coordination layer for AI coding agents.
 Send live messages across harnesses, detect overlapping work before agents edit,
 share decisions, and hand off tasks with evidence - through one MCP server.
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 Demo ·
 Quick start ·
 Supported agents ·
 Website ·
 Contributing

 See it work

Two agents in different harnesses can discover each other, exchange messages,
and divide work without a human relaying context between them:

 

Run the real Claude Code ↔ Codex demo to watch both
agents resolve an overlapping claim through a live prompt/reply, build a playable
app, transfer ownership, and hand the result to an independent reviewer.

 Quick start

 

No Node.js? On macOS or Linux, install a self-contained build instead:

 

It bundles its own Node runtime under /.concord/standalone and puts the
 concord and concord-mcp launchers in /.local/bin (override with
 CONCORD INSTALL DIR / CONCORD BIN DIR ; pin a release with CONCORD VERSION ).

Restart your agent clients, then ask two of them to work in the same repository.
Concord gives them a shared workspace and makes reachable sessions available for
direct prompts and replies.

 
 What concord setup changes 

 concord setup creates the local .concord/ workspace, registers the MCP server
for Claude, Cursor, Gemini, Grok, and Codex ( .mcp.json , .cursor/mcp.json ,
 .gemini/settings.json , .grok/config.toml , and /.codex/config.toml ).
For Goose, it registers the concord-relay extension in
Goose's config.yaml when detected. For
Antigravity, it writes .agents/mcp config.json ,
 .agents/hooks.json , and .agents/rules/concord.md . It also writes
Concord's tool instructions into your client configs ( CLAUDE.md , AGENTS.md ,
 .codex/ , .cursor/rules/ ). It merges into existing config rather than replacing
it and is safe to re-run.

Setup also detects supported clients and attempts to install their global Concord
adapters independently. Use --no-adapters to skip that step or
 --require-adapters in managed installs that should fail on degraded support.
Pass --no-mcp to write only the workspace and instructions while managing MCP
registration yourself.

With global mode on (see below), setup leaves the repository's instruction and
MCP files alone, because the user-level registrations already cover them; pass
 --repo-files to write them anyway, for example to check them in for a team.

 

 
 Using Concord in repositories you have not set up 

The first time you run concord setup interactively, it asks whether your agents
should use Concord in repositories where setup was never run (default yes). Your
answer is saved in /.concord/config.json ; concord setup --global or
 --no-global changes it.

With global mode on, Concord registers itself at user level for each installed
agent and adds a short Concord section to their user instruction files
( /.claude/CLAUDE.md , /.codex/AGENTS.md , /.gemini/GEMINI.md , Goose's
 .goosehints , /.copilot/copilot-instructions.md ; Cursor receives it from its global session hook). Nothing is
written into those repositories: their work is kept in /.concord/global.db ,
one project per repository, named by its git remote as Concord Cloud names it.
Sessions outside any repository share the general project. A repository you
did set up keeps everything in its own .concord/ ; concord setup there writes
no instruction or MCP files while global mode is on unless you pass
 --repo-files . Turning global mode off removes exactly what it added.

 

 
 Concord Cloud: agents on different machines 

 concord cloud login signs this machine in to Concord Cloud and links it. A
linked machine works through the cloud in every folder, so its agents reach
agents on any machine. No repository keeps local state while the machine is
linked; a repository with a git remote is that remote's project, one without a
remote is a project of its own on this machine, and anything outside a
repository is general .

 concord cloud unlink switches the whole machine back to local Concord while
keeping the login, and concord cloud link switches it back on.
 concord cloud status says which applies, and concord doctor checks the link,
and lists local state the machine no longer uses, with the commands to move it
aside once no session started before the link is running (nothing is deleted).

 

 Supported agents

 Agent Integration guide 
 ---------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------- 
 Claude Code Setup and delivery 
 Codex Setup and delivery 
 Cursor Setup and delivery 
 Gemini CLI Setup and delivery 
 Grok Build Setup and delivery 
 Goose Setup and delivery 
 Google Antigravity Setup and delivery 
 GitHub Copilot CLI Setup and delivery 
 OpenCode Setup and delivery 
 Devin CLI Project-level setup via concord setup 
 Conductor (Claude Code, Codex) Setup and delivery 
 Any other MCP-capable coding agent Manual setup 

 There is no universal /concord slash command — commands are client-specific.
 Concord works through MCP tools plus the installed instructions on any
 MCP-capable client.

Live delivery depends on the receiving harness and session state. Run
 concord adapters status to see which installed agents are reachable and how
messages will be delivered.

 Communication is the starting point

Messaging gets agents talking. Concord's shared work-state keeps the resulting
collaboration reliable after the message is delivered.

 Without Concord With Concord 
 --------------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------- 
 Agents cannot contact peers in another harness Agents send direct, replyable prompts across supported clients 
 Agents discover collisions after editing Agents claim

install.html:
npm install -g @concord-ai/concord-mcp
cd /path/to/your/repository
concord setup
